data.narrative:
Umbra, a Series B space and aerospace company founded by David Langan, has raised $100M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers in the sector, with particular relevance to same-stage players including Cowboy Space Corporation ($2.0B Series B valuation), Aalyria ($1.3B Series B), and adjacent-stage comparables Sierra Space ($8.0B Series C) and Skyryse ($1.1B Series C).

Two methods yield quantifiable results. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement to the $100M raised proxy, implying $190M valuation. Peer-median analysis across the four most comparable private transactions yields a median of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied due to absence of revenue disclosure.

Triangulation across these two methods produces a valuation range of $162M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $920M. The material width of this range reflects meaningful dispersion within the peer set and uncertainty regarding Umbra's specific competitive positioning relative to both earlier-stage and substantially larger Series C players. Stage-progression and peer-median methods weight equally in the median estimate. Key uncertainties include actual revenue trajectory, customer concentration, and technical differentiation relative to the cited comparables.
